Testing

Tests are ordinary Faber source. There is no separate test language and no external runner to configure.

A single test#

test declares one test. assert asserts.

+++ toml
locale = "en"

+++ faber
test "additio" {
    assert 1 + 1 ≡ 2
}

Grouping tests#

describe groups related tests under one name.

+++ toml
locale = "en"

+++ faber
describe "arithmetica" {
    test "additio" {
        assert 1 + 1 ≡ 2
    }

    test "multiplicatio" {
        assert 2 * 3 ≡ 6
    }
}

Tagging#

tag labels a test so it can be selected or filtered when running.

+++ toml
locale = "en"

+++ faber
describe "textus" {
    test "concatenatio" tag "fast" {
        assert "a" + "b" ≡ "ab"
    }
}

Modifiers#

Modifiers follow the test name.

+++ toml
locale = "en"

+++ faber
describe "modifiers" {
    test "stable" tag "fast" {
        assert true
    }

    test "every run" repeat 3 {
        assert true
    }

    test "not written yet" todo "waiting on the parser" {
        assert true
    }
}
ModifierMeaning
tag "<name>"Label for selection and filtering
repeat <n>Run the test n times; it passes only if every run passes
flaky <n>Rejected by faber test: flaky retries are not run, so the case fails without running its body
todo "<reason>"Expected-pending; documents why it does not run yet
skipSkip

repeat is a test modifier, not a loop, and it does not retry until a run passes. For loops see Loops.

Asserting#

assert takes any boolean expression.

+++ toml
locale = "en"

+++ faber
describe "assertiones" {
    test "comparisons" {
        assert 1 + 1 ≡ 2
        assert 3 ≻ 2
        assert "abc".length() ≡ 3
    }
}

Tests in the program's own file#

Since 1.19 a source file can carry its tests, and the output a run should print, in sections after its program. Each section starts with a whole-line marker: +++ toml for the header, +++ faber for the program, `+++ faber test for the tests, and +++ text stdout (or stdin, stderr; also json`, jsonl, base64) for streams. A section runs to the next marker.

+++ toml
locale = "en"

+++ faber
@ public
fn double(int x) → int {
    return x * 2
}

main {
    print double(21)
}

+++ faber test
test "doubles" {
    assert double(21) ≡ 42
}

+++ text stdout
42

The test section sees the program's @ public items, as a sibling file would. check, run and build compile only the program section; faber test runs the test section, and faber corpus compares the program's output with the stream sections. A file with only a +++ faber test section is a test-only file that faber test runs and faber run refuses.

Where tests live, and running them#

Tests let beside the code they exercise, inside the package. Run them with:

faber test <package>
